result:
I can't tell you the exact cause without your data. The most likely explanation is that your reviews look different from the training data, and short reviews fit 68% well.

**My 93.07% wasn't caused by leakage.** No eval review appears in the training data. Only 9 of the 404 eval reviews share even one 8-word phrase with a training review, and none share five.

**But 93.07% was on the lucky side.** In 5-fold cross-validation on `data.csv`, folds ranged from 86% to 93%, with a mean of **88.4%**. A fairer figure for this kind of data is about 88%.

**Most of the remaining gap is very likely a mismatch between your data and the training data.** All of the training and eval data looks the same: roughly 150-word passages taken from longer movie reviews (median exactly 150 words, often starting mid-sentence). Both splits come from that one source, so the 93% only tells you how the model does on more of the same. When I cut the eval reviews short, accuracy drops sharply:

| Words kept per review | Eval accuracy |
|---|---|
| 150 (full) | 93.1% |
| 80 | 87.4% |
| 40 | 81.4% |
| 20 | 71.0% |
| 10 | 64.4% |

Your 68.4% falls between the 10- and 20-word results. A word-count model needs many words to outvote odd individual weights, like "good" leaning negative, which the earlier tests found. The other likely shift is topic: products, restaurants or tweets use different words from film criticism, and a model trained on 2,000 movie review passages has no useful weights for those words.

One thing to rule out quickly: check that your labels are exactly lowercase "positive" and "negative". Something like `Positive` or `1/0` would make every comparison fail, so you'd see 0% or around 50%. That probably isn't the cause here, since 68% is too high for it.

**To pin it down, I'd need one of these:**
- Your held-out file (or a sample of it). I can then compare length, topic and vocabulary, and break accuracy down by review length.
- Or just a description: average review length, and what the reviews are about.

**Likely fixes, depending on the cause:**
- **Shorter texts or another topic:** add labeled examples from your own data to the training set. That will help more than any tuning.
- **No such data available:** a small pretrained sentence-embedding model with a linear classifier on top would handle short reviews and other topics much better. It's still CPU-friendly, though slower than TF-IDF.

I'd also update the README to give about 88% on in-domain data, with a note that it only holds for long movie review passages. Shall I make that change?
